title: Water in Fuel Sensor Circuit Low
shortDescription: Water-in-fuel sensor signal low — water in separator or open circuit.
fullDescription:
Detroit Diesel SPN 97 FMI 5 on DD13/DD15/DD16 engines indicates the water-in-fuel sensor circuit is reporting below normal — either significant water accumulation or sensor open circuit.

Drain separator first, clear code. If returns, inspect sensor harness and replace sensor as needed. Water in common-rail fuel destroys injectors operating at 30,000+ PSI.

Daily separator draining is best practice in humid climates or when using bulk fuel storage.

fixSteps.title: Drain separator
fixSteps.instruction: Open drain until clear diesel flows. Close.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With DDDL, monitor WIF status. Disconnect sensor, ohm out per spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap if out of spec. Torque and reconnect.

title: Oil Pressure Below Normal
shortDescription: Oil pressure in low-warning range — check oil first.
fullDescription:
Detroit Diesel SPN 100 FMI 17 on DD13/DD15/DD16 indicates oil pressure below normal warning threshold (typically 15-25 PSI hot idle). ECM derates to protect bearings.

Check oil level first — most common cause. Also check for oil dilution (fuel smell) and sensor accuracy with mechanical gauge.

Detroit engines are sensitive to low oil pressure at hot idle — bearing damage progresses quickly.

fixSteps.title: Check oil
fixSteps.instruction: Level, smell, color. Top off as needed.

fixSteps.title: Mechanical gauge
fixSteps.instruction: Compare ECM reading to mechanical gauge at sensor port.

fixSteps.title: Further diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: If real low pressure confirmed, dealer pan drop / bearing inspection.

faq.a: Fuel smell in oil, rising level between changes.

title: Coolant Temp High (Severe)
shortDescription: Coolant exceeded severe threshold — engine protection engaged.
fullDescription:
Detroit Diesel SPN 110 FMI 0 on DD13/DD15/DD16 means coolant temp exceeded the severe high threshold — typically 225°F+. Engine protection derates or shuts down depending on parameter setting.

Stop immediately, cool, then diagnose. Common causes on DD-series: EGR cooler internal leak (disappearing coolant), plugged radiator, failed fan clutch.

DD15 head gasket repair $10,000+ if ignored.

fixSteps.title: Safe cooldown
fixSteps.instruction: Pull over, idle 2 min, shut down. Wait 30+ min.

fixSteps.title: Level and fins
fixSteps.instruction: Check surge tank. Rinse radiator fins.

fixSteps.title: Combustion gas test
fixSteps.instruction: If coolant vanishes, block test for combustion gases. Positive = head gasket or EGR cooler.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Low
shortDescription: Rail pressure sensor voltage below normal.
fullDescription:
Detroit SPN 157 FMI 4 on DD-series common rail engines indicates rail pressure sensor signal below expected. Sensor, harness, or actual low pressure.

Common rail pressure is 30,000+ PSI. Never work on a running system. Wait 10+ min after shutdown. Skin injection risk — ER immediately if exposed.

Swap sensor first before HPFP diagnosis — sensors are $300, pumps $4,000+.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe 5V ref, ground, signal at sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clean sensor boss before removal. Torque to spec.

title: DPF Differential Pressure Erratic
shortDescription: DPF delta pressure readings erratic — service needed.
fullDescription:
Detroit DD13/DD15/DD16 SPN 3251 FMI 2 indicates DPF delta-pressure data is intermittent or outside expected plausible range. Often means soot overload or DP sensor/tubes plugged.

Blow out DP sample tubes first, then perform parked regen. If code returns, DP sensor or heavy ash loading.

fixSteps.title: Clear tubes
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect DP sample tubes, blow with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Parked regen
fixSteps.instruction: Initiate via dash or DDDL. 30-45 min safe area.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor if persists
fixSteps.instruction: Swap DP sensor per service procedure.

title: DEF Level Low Warning
shortDescription: DEF below low threshold — refill.
fullDescription:
Detroit SPN 3610 FMI 18 on DD13/DD15/DD16 is first-stage DEF low warning. Refill before derate escalation.

API-certified DEF only. Cycle key + drive cycle clears.

faq.a: Blue cap — never add to diesel tank.

title: DEF Quality Poor
shortDescription: DEF quality sensor detected off-spec fluid.
fullDescription:
Detroit DD-series SPN 3364 FMI 2: DEF quality sensor reports concentration outside the 31.8-33.2% range required by ISO 22241. Usually wrong fluid, contamination, or degraded DEF.

Diesel in DEF: DO NOT START — tow to dealer, $6,000+ SCR damage if started. Water/wrong fluid: drain, flush, refill fresh DEF.

Store DEF below 90°F — heat degrades over time.

fixSteps.title: Diesel test
fixSteps.instruction: Smell/color check DEF. If diesel, DO NOT start. Tow.

fixSteps.title: Flush DEF
fixSteps.instruction: Drain, flush 2-3x with fresh DEF until refractometer reads 32.5%.

fixSteps.title: Dealer SCR check
fixSteps.instruction: If SCR efficiency codes persist, dealer assessment.

title: SCR NOx Conversion Low
shortDescription: SCR efficiency below EPA threshold — inducement will follow.
fullDescription:
Detroit DD-series SPN 4364 FMI 18: SCR not converting enough NOx. Troubleshoot in order: NOx sensors, DEF dosing, DEF quality, exhaust leaks, catalyst.

NOx sensor pair replacement clears 60%+ of 4364 codes on DD engines. OEM Detroit NOx sensors recommended.

fixSteps.title: Compare NOx live
fixSteps.instruction: DDDL cruise comparison of inlet vs outlet NOx.

fixSteps.title: Dosing test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure ml/min via DDDL. Replace doser if low.

title: Outlet NOx Reading Low
shortDescription: Downstream NOx sensor drift or exhaust leak.
fullDescription:
Detroit SPN 3226 FMI 18: outlet NOx sensor reading below plausibility — typically sensor drift (aging) or exhaust leak upstream of sensor diluting sample.

Replace outlet (and ideally inlet) NOx sensor. Inspect exhaust seals upstream.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust
fixSteps.instruction: V-band clamps upstream tight and sealed.

whenToCallPro: If not familiar with NOx socket.

title: Engine Brake Solenoid Voltage High
shortDescription: Compression brake solenoid circuit shorted to power or failed coil.
fullDescription:
Detroit DD13/DD15/DD16 compression brake solenoid circuit fault. SPN 520 FMI 3 = voltage above normal — harness short or coil issue.

Engine brake disabled as safety. Critical for mountain descents — diagnose and repair before loaded downhill operation.

Valve cover harness oil-saturation and chafing are common on DD15.

fixSteps.title: Remove valve cover
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect internal harness for oil saturation and chafing.

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance. Replace if out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Reassemble
fixSteps.instruction: New valve cover gasket. Torque to spec.

title: ECM Program Memory Fault
shortDescription: ECM EEPROM/flash fault — reflash or module replacement.
fullDescription:
Detroit ECM internal memory fault. Reflash attempt at dealer first; replacement if reflash fails.

Causes: voltage spikes (jump-starts, welding without disconnect), water intrusion, EOL. Always disconnect batteries before welding to prevent.

fixSteps.title: Reflash at dealer
fixSteps.instruction: Detroit ServiceLink attempts current cal reflash.

title: Boost Pressure Low
shortDescription: Intake boost below commanded — leak, VGT, or CAC.
fullDescription: Detroit DD15 boost shortfall. Most common: CAC end tank crack or boot loose. Smoke test first.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize CAC to ~15 PSI, look for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Repair leak
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat boots, torque clamps, or replace CAC.

fixSteps.title: VGT service
fixSteps.instruction: DDDL command test. Clean or replace.

faq.a: No fixed interval; replace when leaking.

title: EGR Delta Pressure High
shortDescription: EGR venturi DP above normal — sooted or stuck EGR.
fullDescription:
Detroit DD15 SPN 411 FMI 0: EGR venturi differential pressure too high — sooted, restricted, or plugged sample tubes.

Blow DP tubes first (cheap). Full EGR cleaning if persists. Replace if valve stuck.

fixSteps.title: Clean EGR
fixSteps.instruction: Remove valve and venturi. Brush + intake cleaner.

title: EGR Valve Position Not Responding
shortDescription: EGR valve stuck — not reaching commanded position.
fullDescription:
Detroit DD-series EGR valve stuck. Soot binding is typical cause. Clean or replace.

EGR runs hot — allow cooldown before service. Use new gaskets on reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Clean valve
fixSteps.instruction: Cooldown. Remove valve. CRC + brass brush.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: If not responsive after clean, new valve + calibration.

title: DPF Soot High — Regen Needed
shortDescription: DPF soot above threshold — parked regen required.
fullDescription:
Detroit DD-series DPF soot warning. Perform parked regen in safe area. Escalates to derate if ignored.

Low-load/idle duty cycles accumulate soot fastest. Highway miles weekly help passive regen.

fixSteps.title: Parked regen
fixSteps.instruction: Safe area, brake, neutral, initiate. 30-45 min.

fixSteps.title: Service dosing
fixSteps.instruction: If repeats, test 7th injector via DDDL.
